ranked_facts.why: The presence of a prosthetic mitral valve with an indolent months-long illness is more consistent with infective endocarditis, particularly in the context of a new regurgitant murmur and fever, which is less typical for non-infective endocarditis.

A new onset 2/6 holosystolic murmur, loudest in the apical area of the precordium, suggests valve involvement, which is more characteristic of infective endocarditis than a primary cardiac valve disorder.
